 India A vs Nepal Live Score, ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026: Kumar Kushagra, Tilak Varma centuries power India to imposing 332 against Nepal 
 LIVE NOW Save Share Comments India A vs Nepal Live Score, ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026: Kumar Kushagra, Tilak Varma centuries power India to imposing 332 against Nepal
 THE TIMES OF INDIA | Nov 20, 2026, 19:39:02 IST SUMMARY India A vs Nepal Live Score, ACC Mens Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026: The Rising Stars Men’s Asia Cup presents a significant opportunity for India's next generation of players, with T20 stars Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma among those looking to establish themselves in the 50-over format. 
 India A begin their campaign against Nepal today, with captain Tilak Varma viewing the competition as an important stepping stone towards the senior side ahead of the 2027 ODI World Cup. 
 Fifteen-year-old Sooryavanshi will attract considerable attention after his explosive 94 off 29 balls in the tri-series in Sri Lanka earlier this year. Rinku Singh, who has slipped out of India's T20I setup, will be eager to make a strong case for a comeback, while Ayush Badoni and Shahbaz Ahmed also have points to prove. Badoni was drafted into the squad after Rajat Patidar withdrew. 
 The return of pacers Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav from injuries adds another dimension to the campaign. Other prominent names include Prabhsimran Singh, Suryansh Shedge, Vipraj Nigam, Harsh Dubey and Tanush Kotian. 
 Tilak has encouraged his players to enjoy the occasion, trust their abilities and avoid pressure, stressing that strong performances and match-winning contributions could open doors to international cricket. Commentary 
 Scorecard 
 19:38 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: Tilak, Kushagra centuries power India A to imposing 332 against Nepal India A post a formidable 332/9 against Nepal after recovering from early setbacks to build a massive total. Kumar Kushagra (117 off 102) and skipper Tilak Varma (107 off 113) stitch together a magnificent 206-run partnership, with both batters scoring centuries. 
 Suryansh Shedge provides a late flourish with a blistering 36 off just 14 balls, including three sixes and two fours, as India A breach the 330-run mark. 
 Nepal's Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane claim three wickets each, but India finish with a challenging total on a slow surface.
 18:38 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: Kumar Kushagra's century takes India A past 230 India A continue their dominant charge against Nepal, reaching 237/3 after 41 overs. Kumar Kushagra remains unbeaten on 116 off 99 balls, bringing up his third List A century, while Tilak Varma supports him with an unbeaten 77 off 95 deliveries. 
 The duo adds 16 runs in the 41st over, with Kushagra smashing a six and a four off Sandeep Lamichhane to keep the momentum firmly with India A.
 18:15 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: Tilak, Kushagra Take India A Past 175 Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra continued to strengthen India A’s position with an unbeaten partnership, taking the score to 178/3 after 37 overs against Nepal. The duo added 26 runs across the 34th, 35th, 36th and 37th overs, with Tilak reaching 67 off 89 balls and Kushagra moving to 68 off 81. 
 Tilak struck a six off Sandeep Lamichhane in the 37th over, which yielded 14 runs, while Kushagra also found the boundary through four byes. Their partnership continued to revive India A after the early setbacks.

 17:49 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: Tilak Varma, Kumar Kushagra Hit Half-Centuries To Rescue India A India A reach 142/3 after 32 overs as captain Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra bring up impressive half-centuries to revive the innings against Nepal. 
 The pair complete a 100-run partnership, helping India A recover from early setbacks after losing three wickets inside 11 overs. Tilak scores an unbeaten 50 off 77 deliveries, while Kushagra reaches 53 off 63 balls. 
 Both batters gradually accelerate, with Kushagra finding boundaries and Tilak striking a six in the 32nd over.
 17:33 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: Tilak Varma, Kumar Kushagra Steady India A After Early Wickets India A reach 117/3 after 28 overs as captain Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra lead the recovery with a valuable partnership. After struggling to score freely against Nepal's disciplined spin attack, the duo gradually settle at the crease and find boundaries to lift the scoring rate. 
 Both batters move to 39, with Kushagra particularly impressive through the off-side. Nepal continue to keep things tight, but India A manage 10 runs in the 28th over to gain some momentum.
 17:12 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: India A Struggle To Accelerate Against Nepal India A reach 62/3 after 16 overs as Nepal continue to keep the scoring rate under control. Captain Tilak Varma and Kumar Kushagra remain at the crease but find it difficult to score freely against Nepal's disciplined bowling attack. 
 The spinners exploit a slow surface where the ball holds up, forcing the batters to rely on singles. Tilak moves to 13 off 29 balls, while Kushagra remains unbeaten on 10 off 15 deliveries.

 Tilak moves to 13 off 29 balls, while Kushagra remains unbeaten on 10 off 15 deliveries.
 16:30 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: Nepal Keep India A Under Pressure, Reduce Them To 48/3 India A struggle to find momentum as they reach 48/3 after 12 overs against Nepal. Pawan Sarraf delivers a crucial breakthrough by bowling the dangerous Vaibhav Sooryavanshi for 26 off 32 balls, with the batter failing to adjust to the turn. 
 Earlier, Lalit Rajbanshi dismisses Ayush Badoni through a stumping, leaving India A in trouble. Kumar Kushagra joins captain Tilak Varma at the crease and gets off the mark with a boundary. 
 Kushagra remains unbeaten on five, while Tilak has four as Nepal continue to dominate proceedings.
 16:14 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: Nepal Tighten Their Grip As India A Slip To 39/2 India A struggle to build momentum and reach 39/2 after nine overs against Nepal. 
 Left-arm spinner Lalit Rajbanshi provides the breakthrough by dismissing Ayush Badoni for two, beating him in flight as he steps out and gets stumped. Nepal continue to keep the pressure on with disciplined bowling, restricting the scoring opportunities. 
 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi remains unbeaten on 26 off 29 deliveries, while captain Tilak Varma joins him at the crease on one.
 16:01 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: India A Lose Abhishek Sharma Early After Positive Start India A reach 34/1 after six overs against Nepal, but lose opener Abhishek Sharma for nine off 13 deliveries. Nandan Yadav provides the breakthrough as Abhishek attempts a big shot and gets caught at mid-on. 
 Vaibhav Sooryavanshi keeps the scoreboard moving with an aggressive 23 off 20 balls, including a six and three fours. Ayush Badoni joins Sooryavanshi at the crease, while Nepal's bowlers continue to find assistance from a pitch where the ball holds up.
 15:26 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: Nepal Opt To Bowl Against India A Nepal win the toss and elect to bowl first against India A in their opening match of the ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 in Doha. India A captain Tilak Varma says his side wants to bat first and post a competitive total, adding that the team is confident. 
 Nepal skipper Sandeep Lamichhane feels the pitch looks decent and backs his side to chase successfully. He also reveals that Nepal have only 12 players available due to the ongoing Nepal Premier League (NPL).
 14:53 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: India A Begin Asia Cup Rising Stars Campaign Against Nepal India A begin their ACC Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026 campaign against Nepal in Doha, aiming to end a 13-year title drought after winning the inaugural edition in 2013. Led by Tilak Varma, the squad boasts exciting talents and established names such as Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Rinku Singh, who serves as vice-captain. 
 Harshit Rana also returns from injury to strengthen the pace attack, while four spin options provide variety. Nepal, meanwhile, look to build on their promising T20 World Cup showing as they test their skills in the 50-over format.
 14:34 (IST) Nov 20 India vs Nepal: SQUADS! India A: Abhishek Sharma, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Prabhsimran Singh [WK], Tilak Varma [C], Rinku Singh [VC], Kumar Kushagra [WK], Suryansh Shedge, Shahbaz Ahmed, Vipraj Nigam, Harsh Dubey, Tanush Kotian, Harshit Rana, Prince Yadav, Arshad Khan, Ayush Badoni.
 Nepal: Sandeep Lamichhane (captain), Lokesh Bam, Basir Ahmad, Arjun Kumal, Nandan Yadav, Pawan Sarraf, Lalit Rajbanshi, Kushal Bhurtel, Sompal Kami, Deepak Dumre, Sandeep Jora, Abhishek Gautam, Ishan Pandey, Rashid Khan, Dev Khanal.
 14:24 (IST) Nov 20 NEP vs IND: Harshit Rana's comeback and Tilak's message Harshit Rana's return will be another storyline to follow, with the pacer looking to demonstrate that he has recovered fully after injuries to his hamstring and quadriceps. Prince Yadav is also returning from injury, making the tournament an important opportunity for both fast bowlers to regain rhythm and confidence. Tilak, meanwhile, has urged his players to embrace the occasion rather than allow the prospect of a senior-team opportunity to weigh them down. “There are more than 5 or 7 players who have played in the senior side. If in these conditions and stages you do well after coming here, then why not? You will be high on confidence. This tournament is very crucial for each and every player at the same point,” he said. He added: “I just say to my players that don’t take any pressure, just enjoy and whatever you feel, whatever hard work you have done, you deserve this. So this is a stage where you should not take any pressure because you are already representing India. It’s just a matter of a few performances to go there at the senior level. So I just say that if you enjoy it, then your natural skill comes out and you do well. So that’s where you can go into the senior team as well,” he concluded. 14:24 (IST) Nov 20 IND vs NEP: Rinku, Badoni and Shahbaz have points to prove While the tournament offers a platform for emerging names, it is equally important for some established domestic and international performers looking to regain momentum. Rinku, who has lost his place in India's T20I setup, will be eager to make a strong impression. Ayush Badoni, a late addition after Rajat Patidar pulled out, will look to build on an impressive start to the domestic season and attract the selectors' attention. Shahbaz Ahmed, who last played for India in 2023, also has an opportunity to put himself back in contention. Other familiar names in the squad include Prabhsimran Singh, Prince Yadav, Suryansh Shedge, Vipraj Nigam, Harsh Dubey and Tanush Kotian. Sooryavanshi, Shedge and Dubey were also part of India's A squad in last year's edition, which was played in the T20 format. 14:23 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: 'The standards are really high here' Tilak also pointed out that the presence of senior-level players in the competition would ensure a demanding environment for everyone involved. Several participants have already represented India, while others have performed consistently in domestic cricket and the IPL. The captain believes that doing well against such opposition can provide players with the confidence that they are ready for the next step. “I have played here and done well. This is a big stepping stone in terms of playing international cricket. There are senior players who are playing in opposite teams and in our team as well, including myself, who have played senior cricket and are coming back here. So the standards are really high here,” he said. He added that players must translate their opportunities into match-winning contributions rather than focus only on individual performances. 13:42 (IST) Nov 20 India vs Nepal: Tilak draws from his own IPL breakthrough Tilak's own journey offers an example of how a strong performance at the right stage can change a player's career. His breakthrough came during his first IPL season with Mumbai Indians in 2022, and he believes the confidence gained from performing in a high-pressure environment can prove invaluable. The left-handed batter has since gone on to establish himself in the senior Indian setup and is now the side's vice-captain in T20Is. Drawing on that experience, he described the Rising Stars tournament as an important stepping stone for players aspiring to represent India at the highest level. “I myself have been in this situation in 2022 when I played my first year in the IPL. So it went really well, and from that time onwards, till now, I have been playing,” he said. 13:42 (IST) Nov 20 NEP vs IND: 'This stage will be very crucial' Tilak underlined the importance of the tournament as a platform for players hoping to move closer to the senior side, with the next 10 months particularly significant in the build-up to the 2027 World Cup. He believes the opportunity must be treated as more than just another assignment, with individual performances and the team's overall success both carrying weight. “So I feel that’s why they have got an opportunity here. If they do well here, hopefully, they will get a chance there as well. So this stage will be very crucial. In the next 10 months, we have the World Cup. So I feel it is important for every individual and at the same time, it’s very important to win the tournament,” he said in a video posted on bcci.tv on Thursday. His comments reflect the significance of the competition for players seeking to establish themselves in the 50-over setup. 13:40 (IST) Nov 20 IND vs NEP: Tilak sees tournament as a pathway to senior team India A captain Tilak Varma believes the competition has arrived at an important time for several members of the squad, particularly with the next ODI World Cup approaching. The selectors have included a number of players with senior international experience, giving the tournament a strong competitive edge. Tilak, who was part of India's recent ODI series in New Zealand but did not get a game, will himself be looking to make the most of the leadership responsibility. He believes strong performances in the tournament could help players earn opportunities at the senior level. “If you see, Harshit is coming back from injury, and Prince also is coming back from injury. Then Vaibhav and Abhishek, who have done really well in T20 cricket and are coming back into the one-day setup, it’s really important for them to build on what they have done in T20 cricket,” Tilak said. 13:40 (IST) Nov 20 India A vs Nepal Asia Cup Rising Stars Live: Sooryavanshi's next big opportunity All eyes will be on 15-year-old Sooryavanshi, who has already displayed the temperament to play substantial innings for the India Under-19 and A teams. His explosive 94 off just 29 balls in the tri-series in Sri Lanka earlier this year attracted attention across the cricketing world, but the Rising Stars Asia Cup will provide a different challenge in the 50-over format. The teenager has also recently taken on the responsibility of captaining Bihar in the ongoing Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy. Having made a name for himself with his extraordinary hitting in T20 cricket, Sooryavanshi will be keen to show that he can adapt his game to the demands of a longer format and build innings when required. 13:40 (IST) Nov 20 India vs Nepal: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, Abhishek Sharma face 50-over test Hello and welcome to the live coverage of the Men's Asia Cup Rising Stars match between India A and Nedal.
 Star T20 performers Vaibhav Sooryavanshi and Abhishek Sharma will have an opportunity to strengthen their 50-over credentials when a power-packed India A begin their Rising Stars Men’s Asia Cup campaign against Nepal today. The tournament offers several players in the squad a chance to demonstrate that their abilities extend beyond the shortest format, with the 2027 ODI World Cup less than a year away. Alongside Sooryavanshi and Abhishek, the squad features established T20 names such as captain Tilak Varma and Rinku Singh. For some, it is an opportunity to push for a place in the senior ODI setup; for others, it is a chance to revive their international prospects.
